Control Accounts — Amortization Entries

Control accounts for accumulated amortization track the total amortization charged against all intangible assets.

These accounts automatically summarize amortization entries from individual intangible assets into a single contra-asset account on the balance sheet.

Name
Name

The name identifies this control account in your chart of accounts.

Understanding Control Accounts

Control accounts are summary accounts in the general ledger that represent the total accumulated amortization of all intangible assets.

An intangible asset accumulated amortization control account automatically consolidates all amortization entries into a single contra-asset account. This reduces the carrying value of intangible assets on the balance sheet to reflect their net book value.

Naming Conventions

When naming accumulated amortization control accounts, use descriptive names that match the related intangible asset categories:

• Accumulated Amortization - Software

• Accumulated Amortization - Patents

• Accumulated Amortization - Licenses

• Accumulated Amortization - Intangibles

Benefits

Using control accounts provides several advantages:

• Automatic tracking of intangible asset amortization

• Simplified calculation of net carrying values

• Detailed amortization schedules for each asset while presenting consolidated amounts

• Proper matching of costs with revenue generation periods

Best Practices

Create separate accumulated amortization control accounts for each intangible asset control account category.

This approach helps maintain clear relationships between assets and their amortization, distinguishes between different amortization periods, and ensures compliance with accounting standards for intangible asset presentation.

Group
Group

The balance sheet group determines where this control account appears on your balance sheet.

Accumulated amortization accounts are typically placed under the intangible assets section as contra-asset accounts.
